faqs: What areas does Integrity Roofing serve?

We are based in Gilbert and serve the Phoenix Valley, including Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley, Tempe, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Apache Junction, Ahwatukee, Glendale and Peoria. If you're nearby and not sure, call the office at 602-548-3770.
Is Integrity Roofing licensed and insured?
Yes. We are licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC #096629) and are bonded and insured. You can look up any contractor's license on the ROC website before you hire them.
What types of roofs do you work on?

Concrete and clay tile, asphalt shingles, spray polyurethane foam, flat/low-slope systems, elastomeric roof coatings, metal roofing and steep sloped roofs. Many Arizona homes have more than one type — for example a tile roof with a flat foam section over a patio.
Do you work on homes and businesses?
Both. We handle residential roofing for single-family homes and commercial roofing for offices, retail, industrial buildings and multi-family properties.
How do I schedule an estimate?

Call the office at 602-548-3770 (Monday–Friday, 7 am–5 pm) or use the estimate request form on our website. We'll set a time to inspect your roof and then give you a clear estimate for the recommended work.
How do I know if my roof needs repair or replacement?

It depends on the roof's age, the type of material and how widespread the damage is. A single leak or a few broken tiles is usually a repair. Widespread granule loss, brittle underlayment or repeated leaks in several places often point to replacement. An inspection gives you a clear answer.
How long does a roof last in Arizona?

Roughly: asphalt shingles 15–25 years, foam roofs 20+ years with regular recoating, metal 40+ years, and concrete or clay tile 50+ years — but the underlayment beneath tile usually needs replacing after about 20–25 years. Heat and UV shorten lifespans compared with milder climates.
When is the best time to have my roof inspected?
Spring, before monsoon season starts on June 15, and again after any major storm. Fall is also a good time to check for summer heat damage before winter rains.
Do you offer financing?
Yes, financing options are available. Ask about them when we schedule your estimate.
What are your office hours?
Monday through Friday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm. We are closed Saturday and Sunday. Call 602-548-3770 or request an estimate online any time and we'll respond during business hours.
Where is your office?
Our office is at 16308 E Fairview St, Gilbert, AZ 85295.
Can you help after monsoon storm damage?

Yes. Call us during business hours and we will inspect the roof, document the damage with photos, and recommend a repair. If water is actively coming in, move belongings away from the leak and contain the water until we can get there.

faqs: How do I know if my roof is leaking?

Look for water stains on ceilings or walls, peeling paint near the ceiling line, damp insulation in the attic, daylight through roof boards, or a musty smell. Outside, look for broken or slipped tiles, missing shingles, or bubbling on a foam roof.
Can you repair a tile roof without replacing it?

Usually, yes. Broken tiles can be replaced individually, and isolated underlayment problems can be repaired by lifting the tiles in that area. If the underlayment is failing across the whole roof, an underlayment replacement (tile re-felt) may be the better long-term fix.
What causes most roof leaks in Arizona?

Aged underlayment beneath tile, cracked or displaced tiles, worn flashing at walls and penetrations, clogged valleys and drains, and weathered coatings on flat and foam roofs. Monsoon winds and heavy rain expose these weak spots.
How often should I have roof maintenance done?
For most homes, once a year plus after major storms. Foam and coated flat roofs also need recoating on a schedule — typically every several years depending on the coating thickness and exposure.
Is it worth repairing an old roof?

If the problem is isolated and the rest of the roof is in good shape, a repair is usually the smart choice. If you are repairing the same roof again and again, replacement can cost less over time. We'll give you an honest recommendation.
What should I do if my roof is leaking right now?

Move furniture and valuables away from the leak, put a bucket under drips, and if the ceiling is bulging with water, carefully poke a small hole to let it drain into a bucket. Then call us at 602-548-3770 during business hours (Mon–Fri, 7 am–5 pm).
Do you repair roofs you didn't install?
Yes. We repair roofs regardless of who installed them.

roof-replacement-services.lead: When repairs no longer make sense, we replace your roof with the right system for your home or building — from tile underlayment replacement to a full tear-off and new roof.
roof-replacement-services.answer: You likely need a roof replacement if your roof is near the end of its expected life, leaks in several places, has widespread cracked tiles or granule loss, or the underlayment beneath tile has become brittle. In Arizona, tile roofs are often "re-felted" — the tiles are lifted, new underlayment is installed, and the tiles are reinstalled.

sections.body:
"Re-roofing" can mean different things. On a tile roof, it often means removing the tiles, replacing the worn underlayment, and reinstalling the existing tiles (replacing any broken ones). On shingle roofs, it typically means a complete tear-off down to the deck and new shingles. A full replacement may also include new decking, flashing and ventilation.

We'll explain which option fits your roof, what's included, and why.

sections.h2: Signs it's time to replace your roof
sections.body: Age alone doesn't decide it, but these signs mean it's time for a serious look:
bullets: Leaks in more than one area, or the same leak returning
Brittle, torn or exposed underlayment beneath tile
Curling, cracked or bald shingles and heavy granule loss
Sagging roof lines or soft spots in the deck
Foam roof worn through the coating to bare foam
The roof is near or past its expected lifespan

faqs: How long does a roof replacement take?
Most residential roof replacements take a few days once work begins, depending on size, roof type, weather and whether decking needs repair. We'll give you a timeline with your estimate.
What is a tile re-felt or underlayment replacement?

On a tile roof, the tiles themselves can last 50 years or more, but the underlayment beneath them wears out sooner. A re-felt removes the tiles, installs new underlayment, and reinstalls the tiles, replacing any that are broken.
Can a new roof be installed over my old one?
Sometimes on shingle roofs, but we generally recommend a full tear-off so the deck can be inspected and the new roof performs as designed. Tile roofs should not be layered.
Do I need a permit to replace my roof?
Most Valley cities require a permit for re-roofing. Requirements vary by city, and we'll let you know what applies to your property.
Will I need to leave my home during the replacement?
Usually not. It will be noisy during the workday, and we recommend moving cars out of the driveway and keeping pets inside or away from the work area.
How much does a roof replacement cost?
It depends on roof size, pitch, material, the condition of the deck and how many layers need removal. We'll give you a clear estimate after inspecting your roof. Financing options are available.
Which roof type is best for Arizona?

Tile and foam roofs perform very well in Arizona heat; shingles are a cost-effective choice for many homes; metal offers long life and reflectivity. The best choice depends on your home's design and budget — see our roof types page for a comparison.

sections.h2: Why inspect a roof that "looks fine"
sections.body:
Most roof damage isn't visible from the ground. Tiles crack from foot traffic and heat, underlayment dries out under the tiles, and sealants around vents shrink in the sun. By the time there's a stain on the ceiling, the water has usually been getting in for a while.

A routine inspection is the least expensive way to protect the most expensive part of your home's exterior.

features: Cracked, broken, slipped or missing tiles and shingles; foam and coating wear.
Signs of water entry, staining, and soft or damaged decking.
Walls, chimneys, skylights, valleys and roof-to-wall transitions.
Plumbing vents, HVAC, solar mounts and satellite dishes.

faqs: How often should a roof be inspected in Arizona?
At least once a year, ideally in spring before monsoon season begins June 15, and again after any major storm. Older roofs benefit from more frequent checks.
Should I get a roof inspection when buying a home?

Yes. A general home inspector looks at the roof, but a roofing contractor can give you a closer look at the roof's condition, the remaining life, and what repairs may be needed — useful information before you close.
What happens during a roof inspection?
We check the roof covering, flashing, valleys, penetrations, drainage and visible signs of leaks, document what we find with photos, and explain our recommendation.
How long does a roof inspection take?
Most residential inspections take about an hour, depending on the roof's size, pitch and access.
Do I need to be home for the inspection?
It helps if you can be there so we can walk you through what we found, but it isn't always required for an exterior roof inspection. We'll arrange the details when we schedule.
Can an inspection help with an insurance claim?
Our photos and findings document the roof's condition and any damage, which you can share with your insurance company. Coverage decisions are made by your insurer.

sections.h2: Common types of roof damage in Arizona
sections.body: Arizona's monsoon season (June 15 – September 30) brings sudden high winds and heavy rain. Combined with year-round heat and UV, that's a tough environment for any roof.
bullets: Punctures, blisters or exposed foam on flat roofs
Damage from falling branches or debris
Water intrusion from clogged valleys and drains

sections.h2: What to do after a storm
sections.body:
1. Stay safe. Don't climb onto a wet or damaged roof.
  2. Protect the inside. Move belongings away from leaks and contain dripping water.
  3. Take photos. Photograph visible damage from the ground and any interior water stains.
  4. Call us. Phone 602-548-3770 (Mon–Fri, 7 am–5 pm) to schedule an inspection.
  5. Contact your insurer if you plan to file a claim — our photos and findings can help document the damage.

faqs: How can I tell if my roof was damaged in a storm?

From the ground, look for missing or lifted shingles, broken or shifted tiles, debris on the roof, dents in gutters, and granules collecting at downspouts. Inside, check ceilings and the attic for new stains or damp spots.
Should I get on the roof to check for damage?
No. Wet and damaged roofs are slippery, and walking on tile can break more tiles. Let a roofer inspect it.
Will insurance cover storm damage to my roof?

Many homeowner policies cover sudden storm damage, but not wear and tear. Coverage depends on your policy and your insurer's decision. We can document the damage with photos for you to share with your insurance company.
Do you offer emergency or after-hours service?
Our office is open Monday through Friday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm. Call 602-548-3770 during those hours, or request an estimate online and we'll follow up on the next business day.
Can a damaged roof be repaired, or does it need to be replaced?
Most storm damage is repairable. Replacement is usually recommended only when damage is widespread or the roof was already near the end of its life.
How can I prepare my roof for monsoon season?
Have it inspected in spring, replace broken tiles or shingles, clear valleys, gutters and roof drains, trim overhanging branches, and reseal flashing and penetrations.

sections.body: Most commercial buildings in the Valley have flat or low-slope roofs — spray foam, modified bitumen, or coated systems — plus HVAC units and lots of penetrations. Those details are where leaks start.
bullets: Commercial roof inspections and condition reports
Spray polyurethane foam roofing and recoating

sections.body: For property managers, unplanned leaks mean tenant complaints and damaged inventory. Regular inspections and scheduled recoating spread costs out, extend the roof's life, and help you plan capital expenses instead of reacting to emergencies.

faqs: What types of commercial roofs do you work on?
Spray polyurethane foam, elastomeric-coated roofs, flat and low-slope systems such as modified bitumen, metal roofs, and tile or shingle on sloped commercial buildings.
How often should a commercial roof be inspected?
At least twice a year — typically spring and fall — and after major storms. Regular inspections catch drainage and flashing issues early.
Can a commercial roof be recoated instead of replaced?

Often, yes. If the existing roof is structurally sound and mostly dry, a coating or foam recoat can extend its life at a fraction of the cost of replacement. An inspection will tell us if your roof is a good candidate.
Do you work with property managers and HOAs?
Yes. We work with property managers, HOAs and building owners on multi-family and commercial properties.
Can you work around our business hours?
We'll coordinate scheduling with you to minimize disruption to your tenants, customers and operations.
Why are reflective roofs popular on Arizona commercial buildings?
Light-colored, reflective coatings reflect sunlight and reduce heat absorbed by the roof, which can help lower cooling demand in hot climates.

roof-types.title: Arizona Roof Types: Tile, Shingle, Foam & More | Integrity Roofing
roof-types.desc: Compare tile, asphalt shingle, spray foam, elastomeric, flat, metal and sloped roofs for Arizona homes and businesses. Lifespans, pros and cons from a Gilbert roofer.
roof-types.h1: Roof types we install, repair and replace
roof-types.lead: Every roof type behaves differently in Arizona heat. Here's a plain-English guide to the roofs we work on — and how to choose the right one.
roof-types.answer: The most common Arizona roof types are concrete or clay tile (very long-lasting, great in heat), asphalt shingles (cost-effective), spray polyurethane foam (seamless and insulating for flat roofs), elastomeric coatings (reflective protection for flat roofs), metal (long life, reflective), and modified bitumen or other flat-roof systems. Integrity Roofing works on all of them.
roof-types.card_text: Compare the roof systems we work on.

sections.h2: How to choose the right roof
sections.body:
Start with your roof's slope: tile, shingle and metal need a sloped roof, while foam, coatings and modified bitumen are made for flat and low-slope areas. Then weigh budget, how long you plan to stay, the look you want, and your HOA's rules.

We'll walk you through the options that fit your home and give you a clear estimate for each.

faqs: What is the best roof type for Arizona heat?

Tile and spray foam are top performers in Arizona heat — tile because of the air space beneath it, foam because it insulates and is coated with a reflective surface. Metal with a reflective finish also performs well. The best choice depends on your roof's slope and budget.
What is the longest-lasting roof in Arizona?
Concrete and clay tiles can last 50 years or more, and metal roofs 40+ years. Keep in mind that the underlayment beneath tile typically needs replacing sooner — often after about 20–25 years.
What roof is best for a flat roof in Arizona?
Spray polyurethane foam is a popular choice for flat roofs in Arizona because it's seamless, insulating and can be recoated to extend its life. Modified bitumen and coated systems are also common.
Can I switch from shingles to tile?
Sometimes. Tile is much heavier than shingles, so the roof structure must be able to support it. An engineering review may be needed. We can tell you what's involved.
Are shingles a good choice in Arizona?

Yes, for many homes. Asphalt shingles are cost-effective and come in many colors, though Arizona heat and UV tend to shorten their life compared with cooler climates. Lighter colors and good attic ventilation help.
Does Integrity Roofing work on every roof type?
Yes — tile, shingle, foam, elastomeric, flat, metal and sloped roofs, for homes and businesses.

tile-roofs.title: Tile Roof Repair & Re-Felt in Gilbert, AZ | Integrity Roofing
tile-roofs.desc: Concrete and clay tile roof repair, broken tile replacement, underlayment replacement (re-felt) and new tile roofs in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix.
tile-roofs.h1: Tile roof repair, underlayment and replacement
tile-roofs.lead: Concrete and clay tile is the classic Arizona roof — beautiful, durable and great in the heat. The key to a long life is what's underneath the tiles.
tile-roofs.answer: Tile roofs are very durable — the tiles themselves often last 50 years or more — but the underlayment beneath them is the real waterproofing layer and typically wears out after about 20–25 years in Arizona. Integrity Roofing repairs broken tiles, replaces underlayment (re-felt) and installs new tile roofs.
tile-roofs.card_text: Concrete & clay tile repair, re-felt and replacement.

sections.h2: The tile isn't the waterproofing — the underlayment is
sections.body:
Tiles shed most of the water and shade the roof, but the underlayment beneath them is what keeps water out of your home. Arizona heat dries it out over time until it becomes brittle and cracks. When that happens, leaks begin even if the tiles look perfect.

A tile underlayment replacement (often called a re-felt) removes the tiles, installs new underlayment, and reinstalls your tiles — replacing any broken ones.
We work on concrete and clay tile in all common profiles — flat, S-tile and barrel.
bullets: Leak repair and partial underlayment repair

faqs: How long does a tile roof last in Arizona?
Concrete and clay tiles can last 50 years or more. The underlayment beneath the tiles usually needs replacement after about 20–25 years, depending on the material and exposure.
Why is my tile roof leaking if the tiles look fine?
The underlayment under the tiles is the main waterproofing layer. When it becomes brittle or torn from age and heat, water gets through even if the tiles look perfect.
Can broken roof tiles be replaced individually?
Yes. Individual cracked or broken tiles can be replaced. We try to match the profile and color as closely as possible.
Can I walk on my tile roof?
It's best not to. Tiles can crack under foot pressure if you step in the wrong place. Let a roofer handle access.
Can my existing tiles be reused during a re-felt?
In most cases, yes. Intact tiles are removed, stacked, and reinstalled over the new underlayment. Broken tiles are replaced.
What is the difference between concrete and clay tile?
Clay tile is fired clay with color that won't fade; concrete tile is heavier and usually less expensive. Both perform very well in Arizona.

asphalt-shingles.title: Asphalt Shingle Roofing, Gilbert AZ | Integrity Roofing
asphalt-shingles.desc: Asphalt shingle roof repair and replacement in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Wind damage, granule loss and full re-roofs from a family-owned Arizona roofer.
asphalt-shingles.h1: Asphalt shingle roof repair and replacement
asphalt-shingles.lead: Shingles are a cost-effective, good-looking roof for many Valley homes. We repair wind and heat damage and install new shingle roofs built to handle the Arizona sun.
asphalt-shingles.answer: Asphalt shingle roofs typically last about 15–25 years in Arizona, where heat and UV wear them faster than in cooler climates. Signs of a failing shingle roof include curling or cracked shingles, bald spots, heavy granule loss in gutters, and wind-lifted or missing tabs.
asphalt-shingles.card_text: Repair and replacement for shingle roofs.
asphalt-shingles.service_type: Asphalt shingle roof installation and repair

sections.body: Monsoon winds can lift and tear shingles, and summer heat can make them brittle. We replace damaged shingles, reseal lifted ones, and repair flashing and vents so water stays out.

When your shingles are worn out, we tear the old roof off, inspect and repair the deck, and install a new shingle system with new underlayment, flashing and ridge caps. Lighter colors and good attic ventilation help shingles last longer in Arizona.

faqs: How long do asphalt shingles last in Arizona?
Typically about 15–25 years, depending on the shingle quality, color, attic ventilation and exposure. Heat and UV shorten shingle life compared with milder climates.
What are signs my shingle roof needs replacing?
Curling, cracking or brittle shingles, bald spots, granules piling up in gutters, multiple leaks, and a roof that's near the end of its expected life.
Can a few shingles be replaced after a storm?
Yes. Wind damage to a handful of shingles is usually a simple repair, as long as the surrounding shingles are still in good condition.
Are dark shingles bad in Arizona?
Darker shingles absorb more heat, which can raise attic temperatures and speed up aging. Lighter colors reflect more sunlight. Many homeowners balance appearance with heat performance.
Why are there granules in my gutters?
Some granule loss is normal on new shingles. Heavy, ongoing loss on an older roof means the shingles are wearing out and losing their UV protection.

foam-roofing.title: Foam Roofing (SPF) in Gilbert & Phoenix, AZ | Integrity Roofing
foam-roofing.desc: Spray polyurethane foam roof installation, repair and recoating for flat roofs in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Seamless, insulating and built for Arizona heat.
foam-roofing.h1: Spray foam roofing for flat roofs
foam-roofing.lead: Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) is one of the most popular flat-roof systems in Arizona: seamless, lightweight, insulating, and renewable with a fresh coating.
foam-roofing.answer: A foam roof is spray polyurethane foam applied as a liquid that expands into a seamless, insulating layer, then protected with a UV-resistant coating. With regular recoating, a foam roof can last 20+ years. The coating is what wears — when bare foam is exposed, it's time to recoat.
foam-roofing.card_text: Seamless, insulating flat roofs — install, repair, recoat.

sections.body: Foam is sprayed on as a liquid and expands to form one continuous layer with no seams — and seams are where most flat roofs leak. It adds insulation to the roof, and its reflective coating helps keep heat out of the building.
bullets: Lightweight — often applied over existing roofs
Can be shaped to improve drainage

sections.body: Birds, foot traffic, and UV exposure eventually wear through the coating. We repair blisters, punctures and damaged areas, then recoat the roof to restore protection — usually far less expensive than replacement.

faqs: How long does a foam roof last?
With regular recoating, a foam roof can last 20 years or more. The foam itself is durable; the protective coating on top is what needs periodic renewal.
How often does a foam roof need to be recoated?
It depends on the coating type and thickness, typically every several years. An inspection will show if your coating is getting thin or if bare foam is showing.
What are signs my foam roof needs attention?
Exposed yellow or brown foam, cracks or peeling in the coating, blisters, bird pecks, ponding water, and soft spots.
Can foam be applied over my existing flat roof?
Often, yes, if the existing roof is dry and sound. Wet or deteriorated material must be removed first. We'll check during the inspection.
Is foam roofing good for homes or only commercial buildings?
Both. Many Arizona homes have foam on flat sections — patios, additions and garages — and many commercial buildings use foam on the entire roof.

elastomeric-roofing-coating.title: Elastomeric Roof Coatings, Gilbert AZ | Integrity Roofing
elastomeric-roofing-coating.desc: Elastomeric roof coatings for flat and low-slope roofs in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Reflective, waterproof protection that extends your roof's life.
elastomeric-roofing-coating.h1: Elastomeric roof coatings that reflect the Arizona sun
elastomeric-roofing-coating.lead: A quality elastomeric coating adds a flexible, waterproof, reflective layer to flat and low-slope roofs — often extending the life of a sound roof without a full replacement.
elastomeric-roofing-coating.answer: An elastomeric roof coating is a thick, flexible liquid-applied membrane (such as acrylic or silicone) that stretches and contracts with the roof as temperatures change. It waterproofs the surface and reflects sunlight, which helps reduce heat absorbed by the roof. It works best on roofs that are structurally sound and dry.
elastomeric-roofing-coating.card_text: Reflective, waterproof coatings for flat roofs.

sections.body: Arizona roofs can swing dramatically in temperature between day and night. Elastomeric coatings flex with that movement instead of cracking.
bullets: Reflects sunlight to reduce roof heat
Protects foam and other flat-roof surfaces from UV
Can extend the life of a sound roof

sections.h2: Is your roof a good candidate?
sections.body: Coatings protect a roof — they don't fix a failed one. The roof must be dry, solid, and properly prepared: cleaned, repaired, and primed where needed. We'll inspect the roof and tell you honestly if coating or replacement is the right move.

faqs: What is an elastomeric roof coating?
A thick, flexible, liquid-applied coating — commonly acrylic or silicone — that forms a seamless waterproof and reflective membrane over a roof.
How long does an elastomeric coating last?
It depends on the product, thickness applied and exposure. Coatings are typically renewed every several years; thicker applications last longer.
Can a coating stop my roof from leaking?
A coating can seal minor surface issues, but active leaks and wet or damaged areas must be repaired first. Coatings work best on sound, dry roofs.
Does a reflective roof coating lower energy bills?
Reflective coatings reduce how much heat the roof absorbs, which can lower cooling demand in hot climates. Actual savings depend on the building, insulation and HVAC system.
What roofs can be coated?
Foam roofs, many modified bitumen and built-up roofs, some metal roofs, and other low-slope surfaces in good condition.

flat-roofing.title: Flat Roof Repair in Gilbert & Phoenix | Integrity Roofing
flat-roofing.desc: Flat and low-slope roof repair, coating and replacement for homes and businesses in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Foam, modified bitumen and coated systems.
flat-roofing.h1: Flat roof repair, coating and replacement
flat-roofing.lead: Flat roofs are everywhere in the Valley — on commercial buildings, patios, additions and Pueblo-style homes. Good drainage and a healthy surface are what keep them dry.
flat-roofing.answer: Flat roofs aren't completely flat — they're built with a slight slope to drain. Most flat-roof leaks start at seams, flashing, roof drains and scuppers, or where water ponds. Common flat-roof systems in Arizona include spray foam, modified bitumen and elastomeric-coated roofs.
flat-roofing.card_text: Low-slope roofs on homes, patios and businesses.

sections.h2: Flat roof systems we work on
sections.body: The right system depends on the building, the existing roof, and your budget.
bullets: Modified bitumen — durable rolled roofing with a protective cap sheet
Elastomeric coatings — reflective protection over sound roofs
Repairs to seams, drains, scuppers, parapets and flashing

sections.h2: Ponding water is a warning sign
sections.body: Water that stands on a flat roof for more than a couple of days after rain speeds up wear and finds its way into seams. We can improve drainage — for example by adding tapered foam or clearing and repairing drains — as part of a repair or replacement.

faqs: Why do flat roofs leak?
Common causes are failed seams, worn flashing at parapet walls and penetrations, clogged drains and scuppers, ponding water, and coatings that have worn thin from UV exposure.
How long does a flat roof last in Arizona?
It depends on the system: modified bitumen often lasts around 10–20 years, while a well-maintained foam roof can last 20+ years with periodic recoating.
Is ponding water on a flat roof normal?
A little water that evaporates within a day or two is common. Water that stands longer can accelerate wear and should be addressed by improving drainage.
Can a flat roof be converted to foam?
Often, yes. If the existing roof is dry and sound, foam may be applied over it; otherwise the old roof is removed first.
How often should a flat roof be inspected?
At least once a year, plus after major storms. Commercial flat roofs benefit from inspections in both spring and fall.

metal-roofing.title: Metal Roofing in Gilbert & Phoenix, AZ | Integrity Roofing
metal-roofing.desc: Metal roof installation and repair for homes and commercial buildings in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Long-lasting, reflective roofing built for Arizona.
metal-roofing.h1: Metal roofing built to last in Arizona
metal-roofing.lead: Metal roofs are long-lasting, lightweight and reflective, with a clean modern look. They're a strong choice for homes, outbuildings and commercial properties.
metal-roofing.answer: A properly installed metal roof can last 40 years or more. Metal is lightweight, sheds water quickly, and reflective finishes help reduce heat absorbed by the roof. The parts that need attention over time are fasteners, sealants and flashing.

sections.body: Metal roofing stands up well to sun, wind and rain, and its reflective finishes are a good match for Arizona summers.
bullets: Reflective finishes help reduce roof heat

sections.body: Over time, exposed fasteners can loosen and sealants can dry out in the sun. We tighten or replace fasteners, reseal seams and penetrations, and repair flashing so your metal roof keeps performing.

faqs: How long does a metal roof last?
A well-installed metal roof can last 40 years or more, depending on the panel type, finish and maintenance.
Are metal roofs hot in Arizona?
Metal with a reflective finish reflects much of the sun's energy and sheds heat quickly once the sun goes down. Combined with proper insulation and ventilation, metal roofs perform well in Arizona.
Are metal roofs noisy in the rain?
With solid decking and underlayment beneath, metal roofs on homes are typically not much louder than other roofs.
Can metal be installed on any roof?
Metal is designed for sloped roofs. Flat and very low-slope areas are better suited to foam, coatings or modified bitumen.
What maintenance does a metal roof need?
Periodic checks of fasteners, sealants, flashing and penetrations, plus clearing debris from valleys and gutters.

sloped-roofs.title: Sloped & Pitched Roof Repair in Gilbert, AZ | Integrity Roofing
sloped-roofs.desc: Repair and replacement for sloped and steep roofs — tile, shingle and metal — in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler & Phoenix. Experienced, licensed, family-owned roofers.
sloped-roofs.lead: Sloped roofs shed water fast and look great — and they come with their own challenges: valleys, ridges, flashing details, and safe access on steeper pitches.
sloped-roofs.answer: A sloped (pitched) roof is any roof steep enough to shed water quickly, usually covered with tile, asphalt shingles or metal. Benefits include fast drainage, longer material life, and attic space for ventilation. The most common trouble spots are valleys, ridges, and flashing where the roof meets walls.
sloped-roofs.card_text: Tile, shingle and metal on pitched roofs.

sections.body: Steeper roofs move water off quickly, which is a big advantage during monsoon downpours.
bullets: Fast drainage and less standing water
Works with tile, shingle and metal
Attic space for insulation and ventilation

sections.body: Valleys collect water and debris, ridges and hips take wind, and every wall, chimney and skylight needs proper flashing. We focus on these details during repairs and replacements, and we use proper safety equipment on steep pitches.

faqs: What is considered a sloped roof?
Generally, any roof with enough pitch to shed water quickly — typically roofs covered with tile, shingles or metal rather than flat-roof systems.
Do steep roofs cost more to repair or replace?
Steeper roofs can take more time and safety equipment to work on, which can affect cost. Your estimate will reflect your roof's pitch and access.
What are the most common leaks on sloped roofs?
Valleys, roof-to-wall flashing, chimneys and skylights, and plumbing vent penetrations.
Which roofing materials work on sloped roofs?
Concrete and clay tile, asphalt shingles and metal are the most common choices for sloped roofs in Arizona.
Why is attic ventilation important on a sloped roof?
Good ventilation lets hot air escape the attic, which helps protect roofing materials from excess heat and can reduce cooling costs.
